$comment: The one list of schema files (DE-20, docs/deployment-enhancements/DE-20-schema-migrations.md). Entries are in load order. kind: repeatable = idempotent, re-applied when its checksum changes; versioned = run once in a transaction; data = moves or rewrites rows, needs plan + approve; seed = demo data, never run by a deploy. schema/load_schema.py loads every repeatable entry; schema/apply_all_seed.py runs seed_run in order; python -m schema.migrate keeps the ledger.
$seed_run: apply_all_seed.py's order. Schema entries are repeated around the seeds so a seed-only run against an older database still works; environments_schema follows seed_program because its tail seeds rows for the p-* cast.

entries.why: The migration ledger itself (DE-20). First, so every later entry can be recorded.
The social tenant's channel directory + context bindings (chat state is DynamoDB).

The observability sprint schemas. These were never in this list, so a rebuilt cluster came up without the tables the middleware queries by name — observability.approvals, .canary_experiments, .prompt_versions and .prompt_version_meta are referenced across a dozen middleware files, and each page hitting them 500s on a fresh database. They load in sprint order because the later ones ALTER what the earlier ones create.

The prompt CONTRACT columns (kind/tier/contract/owner_email/ eval_pass_rate) that sprint6's prompt_version_meta does not create. Same bug class as the sprint schemas above, but failing softer and so harder to spot: providers/prompt-library.ts `fetchAuroraMeta` SELECTs all five by name and swallows the error, so a cluster missing this ALTER does not 500 — the prompt library just silently degrades to "Bedrock defaults" with every tier and contract blank. Loads directly after the file that creates the table it alters.
Explicit work context links require both work_items and documents.
Pages and whiteboards written inside an initiative (the Docs tab's New menu, the Discussion's /doc Save) require projects and work_items.
The page-thread migration ledger (work_item_comments -> orgiq:work:<id>).
The agentic loop: agent_jobs, agent_findings, graph_proposals. Was applied only by apply_agentic_work.py, so a rebuild left the Work page 500ing on missing tables.
Document uploads via share links (standalone).
Codebases agents work on. References `projects` (orgiq_schema), so it loads after it — and agent_sdlc loads after this, since its change requests reference agent_project_runs.
Separation of duties (DE-43) and versioned per-initiative policy sets (DE-46). Alters agent_project_runs, agent_change_requests and agent_change_gates, so it loads right after agent_sdlc_schema.
The lab loop: fleet memory + human consults for computer-lab agents.

The fleet itself — which computers exist. Standalone (no FKs): the registry it backs is in-process memory, and a cluster missing this table degrades to exactly the old behaviour rather than failing, so it does not gate anything that loads after it.

Versioned devbox policy profiles (DE-40) and the box columns the one lifetime model reads (DE-48). Alters projects (devbox_profile_id) and devbox_boxes (profile_id, profile_version, task_started_at), so it loads after orgiq_schema and devbox_fleet_schema; seeds ('default', 1) idempotently.
Audit of per-run repository tokens the BFF minted (DE-45): run, repo, permissions, expiry, caller — never the token. Standalone, no FKs.
Bots + bot_runs. Loads last: it references agent_projects, agent_project_runs, agent_jobs and projects, and its ALTERs add linkage columns to tables the files above create.
Initiative budget allocations. Loads after agent_bots_schema.sql (spend reads join bot_runs) and orgiq_schema.sql (FK on projects).
Sprints, SME budget grants, work-item cost estimates, maintenance baseline view. Loads last: references people, projects, work_items, bots and bot_runs.
The spend ledger (DE-30): one row per finished task attempt on every run path. FKs projects and budget_grants, so it loads after this.
DE-33: nullable `provider` on spend_entries so a local $0 is distinguishable from a Bedrock $0. ALTERs the table spend_ledger_schema.sql creates, so it loads right after it.

Spend holds (DE-34): the forecast held at dispatch under an advisory lock, settled by the ledger entry for the same attempt. FKs projects and budget_grants like the ledger, so it loads after spend_ledger_schema.sql.

User budgets (DE-54): one monthly allocation + optional hard cap per app user, burn derived from spend_entries.actor_id. FKs app_users and relaxes spend_holds.initiative_id, so it loads after spend_holds_schema.sql.
Hard caps (DE-36): hard_cap_usd on initiative_budgets and budget_grants. ALTERs tables agent_budgets_schema.sql and program_schema.sql create, so it loads after both.

Maintenance reserve (DE-55, folds DE-39): initiative_budgets.maintenance_reserve_usd/allow_floor_spill, bots.essential, spend_holds.essential. ALTERs bots, initiative_budgets and spend_holds, so it loads after spend_holds_schema.sql.

Run controls (DE-35/37/50): agent_project_runs.cutoff, run_limits + run_slots, agent_jobs.initiative_id (backfilled from payload), fleet_switches, initiative_budgets threshold memory. ALTERs agent_project_runs, agent_jobs and initiative_budgets, so it loads after maintenance_reserve_schema.sql.

Budget periods (DE-38): widens initiative_budgets.period (named-constraint replace) to monthly/quarterly/sprint/rolling, adds rolling_days and the carry-over policy, budget_period_closes, and at most one active sprint per initiative (created only when the data allows). ALTERs initiative_budgets and indexes sprints, so it loads after program_schema.sql and the other money files.

The assessment tenant's own tables (docs/assessment-tenant.md). Standalone — no FK into the org graph — so it can load anywhere; kept here so a rebuilt cluster has the tables the Aurora path of providers/assessment.ts will query.
Which app users are on which assessment team (the Communication plane's "My teams"); needs assessment_teams and app_users, so it loads after both.
Review decks for an assessed team (docs/assessment-deck-goal.md). Additive; FKs assessment_teams, so it loads right after it.
Pipeline run report decks (docs/agentic-flows-migration.md slice 3). Additive and standalone (no FK to the run projection).
Orgiq initiative status decks (docs/agentic-flows-migration.md slice 6). Additive and standalone (project_id is text, no FK).
Durable flow runs (docs/agentic-flows-migration.md slice 4a). Additive and standalone.
Social /deck decks (docs/agentic-flows-migration.md slice 5). Additive, standalone (channel is text, no FK).
bot_runs.dispatched_by — who authorized a run, which is what lets the per-SME budget_grants envelope be enforced. Additive ALTER, so it loads after agent_bots_schema.sql creates the table.

work_items estimate provenance — who stood behind a forecast, when, and for which model. Additive ALTER on work_items, so it loads after orgiq_work_items_schema.sql creates the table and after program_schema.sql adds estimated_cost_usd beside it.

A dispatch prepared on a work item and saved for later (the dispatch drawer's Save for later, 2026-10-28). Additive, FKs work_items and agent_projects, so it loads after both — right after the estimate columns it sits beside.

Paired developer machines (compute_nodes, compute_pairing_codes). No FK into the graph — owner_id is a bare app_users sub — so it can load anywhere. providers/local-compute.ts queries both tables by name with no fallback, so a rebuilt cluster without them 500s every pairing and presence call.

Local compute P2 — cost provenance (bot_runs/agent_project_runs model_provider) plus the fencing columns a pull-side claim needs. All additive ALTERs, so it loads after agent_bots_schema.sql, agent_projects_schema.sql, agentic_work_schema.sql and local_compute_schema.sql have created the four tables it touches.

The pipelines tenant's own tables (definitions' recorded versions, the runs it starts — the runbook dry-run — and its config). No FK into any other table: the projection reads the run-shaped tables, nothing here joins them, so it can load last.

The access tenant's model (docs/access-tenant-design.md §3): catalog, requests, steps, SoD policies, events, reviews, plus the additive people.manager_id and the access cast's people rows. Needs people and app_users (orgiq_schema.sql, identity_schema.sql), so it loads late. NOT yet applied to Aurora — a user decision (goal lane E).
Demo org graph. Needs orgiq_work_items_schema first (decision rows fill its columns).
The curated program seed (14 p-* initiatives, sprints, grants, bots). Generated by schema/seeds/generate_program_seed.py; regenerate, don't hand-edit.

environments_schema.sql is deliberately NOT here. Its last statement seeds environments for the p-* cast, and those ids are created by seed_program.sql — which apply_all_seed.py applies, AFTER this script. So on a from-scratch cluster the INSERT could only ever fail its FK on projects ("violates foreign key constraint environments_org_project_id_fkey"), taking this whole loader to exit 1 with every other file already applied. A file whose tail depends on seed rows belongs in the seed script, so that is where it now loads.
Knowledge-base registry rows.

LAST in the seed run: grants SELECT on an explicit allow-list, so every table must exist. The database half of the agents' read-only boundary (docs/readonly-graph-role.md); apply_all_seed.py sets its password from Secrets Manager afterwards. Kind seed because no deploy runs it today.
Drops the retired newsroom tenant's tables and identity rows on a cluster loaded before its removal. Destructive, so it is a data entry: plan, approve, apply.

Moves human work_item_comments into the orgiq:work:<id> chat threads (middleware/src/lib/migrate-work-comments.ts). Runs against the deployed chat tables (`env`; the operator's shell overrides it) and the Aurora vars from middleware/.env.aws. Must be applied before the BFF that reads the thread is deployed.

Reviewed synthetic portrait cast, by canonical ID only. Publish and verify all hosted JPEG hashes first. Preserves custom photos and linked accounts. Assessment contributor JSON lacks canonical identity and is excluded.
